statement: Preserve materials, visual styles, lights, sun settings and render settings through open and save.
notes: Verified against help page "MATERIAL (DXF)". Corrected: MATERIAL, VISUALSTYLE, LIGHT, SUN and render settings pages exist; camera, sky and render-environment storage are not described and need separate rows. statement: Read and write the GEODATA object (design and reference points, north direction, unit scales, scale estimation settings and the coordinate system definition string) and keep it in sync with GEOGRAPHICLOCATION.

Acceptance sketch: Geodata object retains coordinate system code and reference point.

statement: Open a drawing read-only when another session holds it, and manage per-session lock files (.dwl/.dwl2) alongside the drawing.
notes: UNVERIFIED: No Autodesk help page found describing DWL lock files; OPEN documents Open Read-Only/Partial Open Read-Only only. Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: Second open warns file in use and opens read-only; .dwl removed on close.

statement: Create a .bak copy of the previous version on save (ISAVEBAK), autosave at the SAVETIME interval to a temporary name ending in .sv$, and allow recovery by renaming that file to .dwg.

source.ref: About Creating and Restoring from Backup Files

notes: Verified against help page "About Creating and Restoring from Backup Files". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-AE54276F-ACF1-41A1-87EC-56E297CDB067 ; https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-25AF36C1-CA4A-4C1C-8D93-1C4F436C6C25 | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Save; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: SAVETIME 1: autosave file created after 1 minute; .bak created on first save.

statement: Use incremental saves until the estimated wasted space exceeds ISAVEPERCENT (0 forces a full save every time, default 50), then perform a full save that compacts the file.
notes: Verified against help page "ISAVEPERCENT (System Variable)". | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: ISAVEPERCENT 50: save after 50 percent waste performs full save and compacts.

statement: Read and write DWG per the published Open Design Alliance specification, including object map, class section and compressed/encrypted R2004+ sections.
superiority: Format handled by an open implementation with a published conformance corpus.
notes: UNVERIFIED: Row rests solely on the ODA spec PDF (blocked by proxy); Autodesk help describes DWG versions but not internal layout. Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: Parse object map of R2000 file: object offsets equal list produced independently; sections decompress.

statement: On open, detect drawings last saved by an application other than Autodesk or RealDWG-based software and show a warning dialog and/or command-line notice according to DWGCHECK.
notes: Verified against help page "DWGCHECK (System Variable)". Corrected: Autodesk documents this as the DWGCHECK system variable; the names DWGCHECKPASSED and TrustedDWG are not on the page. Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: File saved elsewhere: DWGCHECK shows a notification when enabled.

statement: Save as drawing template (DWT) with a description and measurement unit choice, and as drawing standards file (DWS).

source.ref: To Save a Drawing File as a Different File Type

notes: Verified against help page "To Save a Drawing File as a Different File Type". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-EA61BCE3-1D2C-41C3-8912-2DC28CCFB415 ; https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-25EA8670-D911-425A-B4B3-69F430756CB6 ; https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-5855276B-3F21-4746-B2B1-59591F181FE4 | prior app hint: cand2 app registers SaveAsTemplate; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: SAVEAS DWT writes with description; DWS used by CAD Standards.

statement: The program must collect 3D print settings for selected objects in a 3D Print Options dialog and hand the result to an external print preparation tool if one is installed.
notes: Added from help page "3DPRINT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run 3DPRINT, select a solid; the 3D Print Options dialog opens, and on confirming, the external preparation application is launched if present, otherwise a notice is given.

statement: The program must export selected 3D solids and watertight meshes, including those inside uniformly scaled blocks and xrefs, to an STL file for a print service, converting meshes to solids according to SMOOTHMESHCONVERT.
notes: Added from help page "3DPRINTSERVICE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a solid and a watertight mesh, run 3DPRINTSERVICE and save; an STL file is written containing both and any other geometry in the selection is omitted.

statement: The program must import a 3ds Max file, covering meshes, materials, mappings, lights and cameras, via a file dialog followed by an import options dialog, while excluding keyframe data, smoothing groups and procedural materials.
notes: Added from help page "3DSIN (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run 3DSIN on a 3DS file containing one mesh and a camera; the mesh and the camera are added to the drawing and no keyframe animation is created.

statement: The program must read ACIS SAT text files of any version up to 7.0 and build 3D solid, body or region objects from them.
notes: Added from help page "ACISIN (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run ACISIN on a SAT file holding one block solid; one 3D solid with the same volume is added to the drawing.

statement: The program must export selected 3D solids, regions and bodies to an ACIS SAT text file and ignore other object types in the selection.
notes: Added from help page "ACISOUT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a solid, a circle and a region, run ACISOUT and save; the SAT file contains the solid and region only.

statement: Provide a command that closes the current drawing, offering to save or discard unsaved changes, and requiring SAVEAS for read-only files.
notes: Added from help page "CLOSE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Modify a drawing, run CLOSE, answer discard, and assert the drawing window closes without writing to disk.

statement: Provide a command that closes every open drawing, asking separately whether to save each drawing with unsaved changes.
notes: Added from help page "CLOSEALL (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open three drawings with two modified, run CLOSEALL, and assert two save prompts appear and then all windows are closed.

statement: Provide a command that closes all open drawings except the current one, asking about saving each modified drawing.
notes: Added from help page "CLOSEALLOTHER (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open three drawings, run CLOSEALLOTHER from the second, and assert only the second remains open.

statement: Provide a command that updates legacy hatches and heavy 2D polylines (from before Release 14) to the optimized objects, for hatch, polyline or all, with a Select option to check results visually.
notes: Added from help page "CONVERT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a drawing with a heavy 2D polyline, run CONVERT Polyline All, and assert it becomes a lightweight polyline with the same vertices.

statement: Provide a command that switches 2D polylines between the old heavy representation (with separate vertex objects) and the optimized lightweight representation, chosen with Heavy or Light.
notes: Added from help page "CONVERTPOLY (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run CONVERTPOLY Light on a heavy 2D polyline and assert the result is a lightweight polyline; run Heavy and assert vertex sub-objects exist again.

statement: Provide a command that puts a snapshot of the displayed view on the clipboard so that OLE client applications can paste it as a linked object.
notes: Added from help page "COPYLINK (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run COPYLINK, paste-link into an OLE container, and assert it shows the current view.

statement: DBCCLOSE must close the Select Data Object dialog of the dbConnect Manager.
notes: Added from help page "DBCCLOSE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open the dialog with DBCDEFINELT, run DBCCLOSE; expect the dialog dismissed.

statement: DBCCONFIGURE must open the data source configuration dialog so an external database can be set up for access from the program.
notes: Added from help page "DBCCONFIGURE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run DBCCONFIGURE; expect a dialog to define a new data source connection.

statement: DBCDEFINELLT must open the database object chooser listing link templates, label templates and queries associated with the drawing for use in the current operation.
notes: Added from help page "DBCDEFINELLT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run DBCDEFINELLT in a drawing with one link template; expect the dialog to list it and allow selecting it.

statement: DBCDEFINELT must open the Select Data Object dialog showing the Data Sources tree of the dbConnect Manager so a database table can be chosen for the current operation.
notes: Added from help page "DBCDEFINELT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run DBCDEFINELT; expect the dialog listing configured data sources and tables.

statement: DBCONNECT must open the dbConnect Manager and add the dbConnect menu, giving access to external database tables via the Data View window, Query Editor and Link Select dialog.
notes: Added from help page "DBCONNECT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run DBCONNECT; expect the manager shown and a dbConnect menu on the menu bar.

statement: DBLIST must print database information for every object in the drawing to the text window, pausing when the window fills until Enter, and aborting on Esc.
notes: Added from help page "DBLIST (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a line and a circle, run DBLIST; expect an entry for each with handle, type and layer.

statement: DETACHURL must remove hyperlinks from selected objects and delete the polyline when a hyperlinked area is selected, leaving the URLLAYER layer to be purged separately.
notes: Added from help page "DETACHURL (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Attach a hyperlink to a circle, run DETACHURL and select it; expect the circle to have no hyperlink.

statement: -DGNEXPORT must export the drawing to a DGN file from the command line (V7 or V8) with file name, conversion units (master or sub) and mapping setup prompts, so it can be scripted for batch export.
notes: Added from help page "-DGNEXPORT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run -DGNEXPORT with V8, a path, master units and the default mapping; expect a DGN file created with layers mapped to levels.

statement: DGNEXPORT must write the current drawing to a V7 or V8 DGN file through a file selection dialog followed by an Export DGN Settings dialog, following a documented conversion table of supported DWG data.
notes: Added from help page "DGNEXPORT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run DGNEXPORT, choose a file name and accept settings; expect a DGN file generated from the drawing geometry.

statement: -DGNIMPORT must import a DGN file from the command line, prompting for file name, design model (? lists models), conversion units (master or sub), and mapping setup, so it can be scripted for batch import.
notes: Added from help page "-DGNIMPORT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run -DGNIMPORT with a path, the model name, master units and default mapping; expect the model's geometry added to the drawing.

statement: DGNMAPPING must open the DGN Mapping Setups dialog for creating, modifying, renaming and deleting user-defined mappings from DGN level, line style, weight and color to DWG layer, linetype, weight and color, with a fixed read-only Standard setup listed first.
notes: Added from help page "DGNMAPPING (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a setup mapping level 5 to layer WALLS, use it in -DGNIMPORT; expect imported level-5 objects on layer WALLS.

statement: DIGITALSIGN must sign a drawing with a digital signature using a valid digital ID via the Attach Digital Signatures dialog, and the signature must become invalid if the drawing is changed afterwards.
notes: Added from help page "DIGITALSIGN (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Sign a saved drawing, edit and save it; expect the signature to be reported as invalid or removed.

statement: The program must open a Drawing Recovery Manager that lists backup and recoverable drawing files following a crash or power loss so the user can restore them.
notes: Added from help page "DRAWINGRECOVERY (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: After a simulated crash with an autosave file present, run DRAWINGRECOVERY and assert the backup appears under the Backup Files list and can be opened.

statement: The program must provide a DRAWINGRECOVERYHIDE command that closes the Drawing Recovery Manager.
notes: Added from help page "DRAWINGRECOVERYHIDE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open the recovery manager with DRAWINGRECOVERY, run DRAWINGRECOVERYHIDE, and assert the manager is no longer displayed.

statement: The program must provide a DWG Convert dialog that batch-converts selected drawing files to a chosen drawing format version, with a file list the user can check and manage.
notes: Added from help page "DWGCONVERT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select three DWG files in DWGCONVERT, choose an older format version, run the conversion, and assert all three files are written in that version.

statement: The program must import an AutoCAD DXB binary file, converting its 2D 16-bit vectors into line objects on the current layer with current properties.
notes: Added from help page "DXBIN (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run DXBIN on a DXB file holding three vectors and assert three line objects are created on the current layer.

statement: The program must export drawing objects to other formats chosen in the Export Data dialog, including 3D DWF, ACIS SAT, BMP, block DWG, DXX, EPS, IGES, STL, WMF and DGN, each mapped to its dedicated output command.
notes: Added from help page "EXPORT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run EXPORT, choose STL, select a solid, and assert an STL file is written for it.

statement: The program must provide IGESEXPORT to write chosen drawing objects out to a new .igs or .iges file whose name and location come from a file dialog, and show a notification when processing completes.
notes: Added from help page "IGESEXPORT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Select a 3D solid, run IGESEXPORT and name it part.igs, and assert an IGES file is written and a completion notification is displayed.

statement: The program must provide IGESIMPORT to bring the contents of an IGES file (.igs or .iges) into the open drawing, processing in the background when it takes more than about five seconds, showing a status indicator, and inserting the data when the user follows the completion notification.
notes: Added from help page "IGESIMPORT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run IGESIMPORT on a sample IGES file with a surface, assert import runs without blocking drawing edits when slow, and assert following the notification inserts the geometry.

statement: The program must provide an import command that opens a file picker and translates files from other formats (such as 3DS, ACIS SAT, DGN, IGES, PDF, Parasolid, Inventor, CATIA, Creo and Rhino) into entities in the current drawing, delegating to the format-specific import commands where they exist.
notes: Added from help page "IMPORT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run IMPORT and select a .sat file; ACIS solids appear in the current drawing, and selecting a .pdf routes to the PDF import behavior.

statement: The program must save the current model viewport or the whole paper-space layout display as a slide file, excluding off-screen portions and off or frozen layers.
notes: Added from help page "MSLIDE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run MSLIDE on a viewport containing a frozen-layer object and confirm the created slide omits that object.

statement: The program must create a new drawing, showing either a startup dialog or a template file selector depending on the startup setting, and a command-line prompt when file dialogs are disabled.
notes: Added from help page "NEW (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: With the startup setting at 0, run NEW and confirm a template selection dialog appears; with FILEDIA 0 confirm a text prompt appears.

statement: -PARTIALOAD must load additional geometry from the command line into a drawing that was opened partially, selecting it by rectangular area, named view or layer list, optionally with xrefs unloaded.
notes: Added from help page "-PARTIALOAD (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Partially open a drawing with one layer, run -PARTIALOAD for a second layer and assert its entities now exist in the database.

statement: PARTIALOAD must open the Partial Load dialog so that a partially opened drawing can bring in extra geometry by view or layer, and the loaded data must not be removable even by UNDO.
notes: Added from help page "PARTIALOAD (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Partially open a drawing, run PARTIALOAD to add a view, then run UNDO and assert the loaded geometry stays.

statement: PARTIALOPEN must open a drawing while loading only the geometry and named objects from a chosen view (or extents) and chosen layers, prompting at the command line when FILEDIA is 0 and optionally leaving xrefs unloaded.
notes: Added from help page "PARTIALOPEN (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run PARTIALOPEN on a two-layer drawing selecting only layer A and assert only layer A entities are in the opened drawing.

statement: PNGOUT must save the selected objects, as displayed on screen including light glyphs, to a PNG raster file chosen in a file dialog or at the prompt when FILEDIA is 0.
notes: Added from help page "PNGOUT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run PNGOUT on a circle and assert the output PNG file exists with dimensions matching the display of the selected area.

statement: PURGEAECDATA must remove invisible AEC custom data (Architecture/Civil 3D objects) from the drawing after a Yes/No confirmation, refusing to run if the drawing has attached xrefs or contains visible AEC objects.
notes: Added from help page "PURGEAECDATA (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: In a drawing with only invisible AEC proxy data and no xrefs, run PURGEAECDATA and answer Yes; the AEC data is gone, while with an attached xref the command does nothing.

statement: QNEW must start a new drawing from the default QNEW template configured in Options (Files), falling back to the Select Template dialog when none is set, with behavior governed by STARTUP and FILEDIA.
notes: Added from help page "QNEW (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: With a default QNEW template set to metric.dwt, run QNEW; a new drawing opens with metric.dwt's units and layers, and with the template set to None the template-selection dialog appears.

statement: QSAVE must save the current drawing in the default file format without asking for a name when it is already named, show the Save As dialog when it is unnamed, and choose incremental or full save according to ISAVEPERCENT.
notes: Added from help page "QSAVE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Modify a named drawing and run QSAVE; the file on disk updates with no prompt, whereas in an unnamed drawing QSAVE opens the Save Drawing As dialog.

statement: QUIT must exit the application, prompting to save or discard changes when the drawing has been modified since the last save.
notes: Added from help page "QUIT (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a line and run QUIT; a save/discard prompt appears, and choosing Discard exits without writing the file.

statement: RECOVER must repair and open a damaged DWG, DWT or DWS file, extracting as much data as possible and reporting results in the text window (DXF files are simply opened), with a ~ option to force the file dialog when FILEDIA is 0.
notes: Added from help page "RECOVER (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run RECOVER on a DWG with a corrupted object table; the drawing opens with the intact entities and a recovery report is listed in the text window.

statement: RECOVERALL must recover or audit a damaged drawing together with every attached and nested xref, resave each in the current format with a BAK copy of the original, and show a per-file expandable recovery log that can be copied to the clipboard.
notes: Added from help page "RECOVERALL (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run RECOVERALL on a drawing with one xref that has errors; both files are repaired and resaved, .bak copies exist, and the log shows two collapsible sections.

statement: The command-line -RENAME must rename a named object by prompting for its type (layers, blocks, text styles, dimension styles, table styles, multileader styles, linetypes, materials, UCS, views, viewports and others), old name and new name.
notes: Added from help page "-RENAME (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run -RENAME, choose Layer, old 'WALLS', new 'A-WALL'; the layer list shows A-WALL and objects on it keep their assignment.

statement: RENAME must open a dialog to change the names of named objects, for example text styles, table styles, dimension styles and layers.
notes: Added from help page "RENAME (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run RENAME, pick Layers, select 'WALLS' and enter 'A-WALL'; the layer is renamed.

statement: The program must provide SAVE to write a copy of the current drawing to a user-chosen name or location without changing the current drawing's name, except for a never-saved drawing, which takes the new name.
notes: Added from help page "SAVE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a saved drawing, run SAVE to a new file name, and assert the new file exists while the active drawing keeps its original name.

statement: The program must provide SAVEAS to save the current drawing under a new name or location in a chosen file format so that the new file becomes the current drawing.
notes: Added from help page "SAVEAS (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run SAVEAS to a new name and version, and assert the file is written and the drawing's name now equals the new file.

statement: The program must provide SECURITYOPTIONS to open the Security Options dialog that restricts the running of executable files and code in the program.
notes: Added from help page "SECURITYOPTIONS (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run SECURITYOPTIONS, enable the restrict-executables setting, and assert loading an untrusted executable file is refused.

statement: The program must provide SIGVALIDATE to show the digital signature information attached to a drawing file in the Validate Digital Signatures dialog.
notes: Added from help page "SIGVALIDATE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a digitally signed drawing, run SIGVALIDATE, and assert the dialog shows the signer and whether the file is unmodified since signing.

statement: The program must provide STANDARDS to associate a drawing with one or more DWS standards files using the Configure Standards dialog and its plug-ins for named object types.
notes: Added from help page "STANDARDS (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Associate a DWS file with the drawing, run STANDARDS, and assert the standards file is listed as associated.

statement: The program must provide STLOUT to export 3D solids and watertight meshes to a stereolithography .stl file.

statement: The program must provide the command-line -UNITS to set unit display type (scientific, decimal, engineering, architectural, fractional), precision and angle format for coordinates, distances and angles.

statement: The program must report who has a given drawing open, giving its full path, the date and time it was opened, the computer name and the user login name, using the temporary lock-info file that is removed on close.

statement: The program must import a Windows metafile's vector content as a block reference, prompting for insertion point, scale or corner scaling, XYZ scales and rotation.

statement: The program must open a dialog for setting how Windows metafiles are imported by WMFIN.

statement: The program must save selected objects to a Windows metafile chosen in a file dialog.

statement: Dino 8 must support slide files as view-only snapshots of the current viewport (or all visible paper-space viewports) that omit hidden layers, can be displayed temporarily over the drawing without becoming drawing content, and can be used for presentations or image-tile menus.

Acceptance sketch: Create two named lights, save to DXF, reload, and assert the LIGHTLIST holds two entries whose names and handles match the light objects.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip MLINESTYLE objects, preserving the style name (2), bit-coded flags (70) such as fill, miters and cap options, and the per-element offsets, colors and linetypes.
notes: Added from help page "MLINESTYLE (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Define a multiline style with fill on and round start caps, round-trip via DXF, and assert the name, flag bits and element list match.

statement: DXF import/export must read and preserve OBJECT_PTR objects, which carry owner/reactor links and ASE extended data (1001).
notes: Added from help page "OBJECT_PTR (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Load a DXF containing an OBJECT_PTR with ASE xdata, save it again, and assert the object and its 1001 xdata block are still present.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip PLOTSETTINGS objects, preserving the page setup name (1), plotter or config name (2), paper size (4), plot view name (6), unprintable margins (40-43) and the remaining plot configuration.
notes: Added from help page "PLOTSETTINGS (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a named page setup with a given paper size and margins, save to DXF, reload, and assert those values in the PLOTSETTINGS object are unchanged.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip RASTERVARIABLES objects, preserving the class version (90), image frame flag (70), display quality (71) and insertion units (72) stored in the ACAD_IMAGE_VARS dictionary.
notes: Added from help page "RASTERVARIABLES (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set image frames off and quality to draft, save to DXF, reload, and assert 70 and 71 hold the same values.

statement: DXF import/export must support the render-related objects grouped under this topic (MENTALRAYRENDERSETTINGS, RENDERENVIRONMENT, RENDERGLOBAL, RAPIDRTRENDERENVIRONMENT and RAPIDRTRENDERSETTINGS) so that rendering configuration survives a DXF round trip.
notes: Added from help page "RENDER (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Round-trip a drawing containing each of the five render object types and assert all five are present in the output OBJECTS section.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip MENTALRAYRENDERSETTINGS objects, keeping the legacy render settings (class version, preset name, materials flag and subsequent codes) even though the renderer itself is retired.
notes: Added from help page "MENTALRAYRENDERSETTINGS (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Load a DXF with a MENTALRAYRENDERSETTINGS object, save it, and assert the preset name (1) and materials flag (290) are written back unchanged.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip RENDERENVIRONMENT objects, preserving the fog enabled flags (290), fog color RGB (280), near/far fog density (40) and the remaining environment parameters.
notes: Added from help page "RENDERENVIRONMENT (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Enable fog with a given color and densities, round-trip via DXF, and assert the flags, color channels and both densities are equal.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip RENDERGLOBAL objects, preserving the render procedure (0 for view, 1 for crop, 2 for selection), the destination (render window or viewport), the flag for saving to a file together with its file name (1), the image width and height, and the predefined preset flag.
notes: Added from help page "RENDERGLOBAL (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set render destination to viewport with a 1920x1080 output file, save to DXF, reload, and assert those codes match.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip RAPIDRTRENDERENVIRONMENT objects in the ACAD_BACKGROUND dictionary, preserving the environment flag (290), image-based-lighting map file name (1), IBL rotation angle (40) and IBL-as-background flag.
notes: Added from help page "RAPIDRTRENDERENVIRONMENT (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Enable an IBL map with a 45 degree rotation, round-trip via DXF, and assert the file name, flag and angle are unchanged.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip RAPIDRTRENDERSETTINGS objects, preserving the preset name (1), the materials, texture sampling, back-face and shadow flags (290) and the preview image file name.
notes: Added from help page "RAPIDRTRENDERSETTINGS (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Define a render preset with shadows enabled and materials disabled, save to DXF, reload, and assert the name and each flag value.

statement: DXF import/export must support the section-related objects grouped under this topic (section manager, section settings, section type settings and section geometry settings) so live-section configuration survives a round trip.
notes: Added from help page "SECTION (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Round-trip a drawing with a section plane and assert a SECTIONMANAGER and SECTIONSETTINGS object are written and re-read.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip SECTIONMANAGER objects, preserving the full-update flag (70), section count (90) and the soft-pointer references (330) to each section entity.
notes: Added from help page "Section Manager (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create two section planes, save to DXF, reload, and assert the manager reports 90=2 with both section handles.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip SECTIONSETTINGS objects, preserving the section type (90), the number of generation settings (91) and the type settings that follow.
notes: Added from help page "Section Settings (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Save a drawing whose section object has custom generation settings, reload, and assert 90, 91 and the nested type settings are unchanged.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip section type settings, preserving the section type (90), generation option flag (91), source object references (92/330), destination block (331) and file name (1), and the begin/end markers around the nested geometry settings.
notes: Added from help page "Section Type Settings (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set a section to generate to a destination block from two source solids, round-trip via DXF, and assert the source handles and destination handle are preserved.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip section geometry settings, preserving color, layer, linetype and its scale, plot style, lineweight, face and edge transparency, and hatch pattern type, name, angle, scale and spacing.
notes: Added from help page "Section Geometry Settings (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Customise section geometry with a layer, 50 percent face transparency and a hatch angle, save to DXF, reload, and assert each value.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip SORTENTSTABLE objects, preserving the owner block (model or paper space), the entity references (331) and their sort handles (5), so draw order is retained.
notes: Added from help page "SORTENTSTABLE (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Send one entity to the back, round-trip via DXF, and assert the sort table orders its handle first and regenerated draw order matches.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip SPATIAL_FILTER objects used for clipped references, preserving the clip boundary point count (70, 2 for rectangular, more for polyline) and the boundary points (10/20) with the remaining clip parameters.
notes: Added from help page "SPATIAL_FILTER (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Clip an xref with a rectangular boundary, save to DXF, reload, and assert 70=2 and the two corner points are unchanged.

statement: DXF import must accept SPATIAL_INDEX objects (timestamp 40, always written empty) and may ignore their content, while export writes an empty index.
notes: Added from help page "SPATIAL_INDEX (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Load a DXF containing a SPATIAL_INDEX and assert it opens without error and the drawing geometry is unaffected.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip SUNSTUDY objects, preserving the version (90), setup name (1), description (2), output type (70), sheet set name and subset fields for sheet set output, and the date/time input arrays.
notes: Added from help page "SUNSTUDY (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Define a sun study with sheet-set output and a date list, save to DXF, reload, and assert name, description, output type and the date count.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip TABLESTYLE objects, preserving the version (280), description (3), flow direction (70), flags (71), margins and the per-row-type cell style data.
notes: Added from help page "TABLESTYLE (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a table style with upward flow direction, round-trip via DXF, and assert code 70=1 and the description are unchanged.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip UNDERLAYDEFINITION entries for PDF, DGN and DWF underlays, preserving the underlay file path (1) and underlay name (2).
notes: Added from help page "UNDERLAYDEFINITION (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Attach a PDF underlay, save to DXF, reload, and assert the definition keeps the path and page name.

statement: DXF import/export must preserve VBA_PROJECT objects, writing the binary project data length (90) and the chunked binary data records (310) without alteration.
notes: Added from help page "VBA_PROJECT (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Load a DXF with a VBA_PROJECT of several 310 chunks, save it, and assert the 90 byte count and concatenated binary data are identical.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip VISUALSTYLE objects, preserving description (2), type (70), face lighting model, quality and color mode (71-73) and the remaining face, edge and display settings.
notes: Added from help page "VISUALSTYLE (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a custom visual style with Gooch face lighting, save to DXF, reload, and assert code 71 equals 3.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip WIPEOUTVARIABLES objects, preserving the class version (90) and the display-frame flag (70).
notes: Added from help page "WIPEOUTVARIABLES (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Turn wipeout frames off, save to DXF, reload, and assert code 70 is 0.

statement: DXF import/export must round-trip XRECORD objects, preserving the duplicate-record cloning flag (280) and the arbitrary ordered group codes in the range 1 to 369 without size or order limits.
notes: Added from help page "XRECORD (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Store an xrecord with mixed string, integer and real groups in a specific order, round-trip via DXF, and assert the sequence and values are identical.

statement: DXF export must write a THUMBNAILIMAGE section only when a preview image is saved, and import must accept its presence or absence.
notes: Added from help page "About the DXF THUMBNAILIMAGE Section"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Save a DXF with the preview option on and assert a THUMBNAILIMAGE section exists; with it off, assert it is absent.

statement: DXF import/export must read and write the THUMBNAILIMAGE section content as a byte count (90) followed by preview image data in 310 records of at most 256 characters per line.
notes: Added from help page "THUMBNAILIMAGE Section Group Codes (DXF)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Save a thumbnail of known bytes, reload, and assert the 90 count matches and the 310 records concatenate to the same image.

statement: New drawings must start from a template (DWT) holding default settings, styles and objects, with a selectable template list at startup and the ability to save any drawing as a template.
notes: Added from help page "About Drawings and Templates"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Save a drawing with a custom layer and text style as a DWT, create a new drawing from it and assert the layer and style are present.

statement: Drawing coordinates must be dimensionless drawing units whose display style (decimal, engineering, architectural, fractional, scientific) is configurable without changing stored geometry.
notes: Added from help page "About Units of Measurement"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a line of length 12, switch the display to architectural units and assert it reads 1'-0" while the stored length remains 12.

statement: Linear and angular units must be displayable with selectable formats and precision, with configurable angle direction (clockwise or counterclockwise) and zero-angle base direction, applied in the Properties palette, dynamic input and status bar.
notes: Added from help page "About Unit Format Conventions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Set angular units to degrees/minutes/seconds with clockwise positive and base angle North, enter a 90 degree angle and assert the resulting direction and displayed format.

statement: Opening drawings must support DWG, DWT and DWS files, show a trusted-file indicator, and warn when a drawing from a non-Autodesk source is opened while DWGCHECK is on.
notes: Added from help page "About Opening Drawings"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a DWG written by a third-party tool with DWGCHECK=1 and assert a warning is displayed, while a Dino-written file shows the trusted indicator.

statement: Saving must write DWG in the current or a chosen format, save selected objects to a new file, create backup copies of the previous version, and support automatic saves.
notes: Added from help page "About Saving Drawings"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Save a drawing twice and assert a .bak file holds the first version; set an autosave interval and assert an autosave file appears.

statement: The program must detect damaged drawings, report diagnostics to an error log, and recover as much data as possible on open or via recover and audit commands.
notes: Added from help page "About Repairing Damaged Drawing Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Open a deliberately corrupted DWG and assert a recovery notice appears, the salvageable entities load, and an error log entry is written.

statement: After an abnormal termination the program must save the current work to a _recover file and open a Drawing Recovery Manager at next startup listing drawing files from the crashed session for resolution.

source.ref: About Recovering from a System Failure

notes: Added from help page "About Recovering from a System Failure"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Kill the process with unsaved edits, restart and assert the Drawing Recovery Manager lists the drawing with its recovered and autosave versions.

statement: The program must support drawing standards files (DWS) defining named-object conventions (layers, text styles and similar) and check working drawings against them, reporting and fixing violations.
notes: Added from help page "About CAD Standards"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Associate a DWS requiring layer WALL, run a standards check on a drawing using layer WALLS and assert a violation with a replace fix is reported.

statement: The program must read and write DXF files in ASCII and binary forms and read DXB files, converting between DXF/DXB and DWG on open and save.

source.ref: About Importing and Exporting DXF Files

notes: Added from help page "About Importing and Exporting DXF Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Export a drawing to ASCII DXF, reopen it and assert entity counts and properties match; open a DXB file and assert its vectors are imported.

statement: The program must import V7 and V8 DGN files (even without a .dgn extension), translating basic data to DWG equivalents with options for text, external references and unit conversion.
notes: Added from help page "About Importing MicroStation DGN Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Import a V8 DGN with a reference file and text elements under chosen options and assert elements become DWG entities with units converted accordingly.

statement: The program must export drawings to V7 and V8 DGN with a standard mapping and options controlling external references, master and sub unit ranges, and acceptance of nonzero Z coordinates.
notes: Added from help page "About Exporting MicroStation DGN Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Export a drawing with an xref to V8 DGN with flattening off and assert the DGN contains the 3D coordinates and a referenced file entry.

statement: The program must import WMF vector data and text as blocks (IMPORT, WMFIN) with options such as solid fills configured by WMFOPTS, and export drawing objects to WMF.

source.ref: About Importing and Exporting WMF Files

notes: Added from help page "About Importing and Exporting WMF Files"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Import a WMF clip with the wireframe option and assert a block containing lines and text is inserted; export selected objects to WMF and assert the file is created.

statement: Dino 8 must purge unreferenced definitions such as layers, blocks, linetypes and styles, with the understanding that erasing objects leaves definitions behind, to reduce file size and improve performance.

source.ref: About Purging Unreferenced Layers, Blocks, and Style Definitions

notes: Added from help page "About Purging Unreferenced Layers, Blocks, and Style Definitions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Define a block never inserted, run PURGE and assert the block definition is removed; assert a block that is inserted is retained.

statement: Dino 8 must output a model to a nearby printer or an online printing service by converting solids and meshes to a triangulated binary STL file.
notes: Added from help page "About Printing 3D Models"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run the 3D print service on a sphere solid and assert a binary STL file of triangular facets is written.

statement: Dino 8 must let users sign a drawing file digitally and let recipients verify the signer and whether the file changed after signing.
notes: Added from help page "About Digital Signatures For Drawings"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Sign a drawing, validate it as intact, modify one byte, and assert validation reports the file changed since signing.
